newsitem.title: USA: Crowds gather for New York St Patrick's Day parade.
newsitem.headline: Crowds gather for New York St Patrick's Day parade.

text.p: Enthusiastic crowds sporting Irish-inspired garb from green socks to emerald top hats lined New York City's Fifth Avenue on Monday for the 236th St. Patrick's Day parade.

The sidewalks along the parade route filled early with onlookers wearing shamrocks painted on their faces and waving Irish flags. An estimated 200,000 marchers and more than a million onlookers were expected.

The day honouring the Irish began with a traditional mass at St. Patrick's Cathedral led by Roman Catholic Cardinal John O'Connor. He urged generosity toward immigrants and the poor, in whom one could see "the faces and the voices of our ancestors."
Before joining the parade up Fifth Avenue, which was decorated with a green line up the centre, Mayor Rudolph Giuliani officiated at a wedding at Gracie Mansion, the mayor's residence.

The bride was Davina Ismail-Massey, a London woman who contacted a New York City radio station in January saying she was having trouble arranging a March wedding at City Hall. Giuliani, who appears on a programme on the radio station, WCBS, offered to marry Ismail-Massey and Tyrone Giblin at a St. Patrick's Day breakfast at Gracie Mansion.
The mayor, wearing a shiny green tie, planned to divide his time marching with the New York City Police Department, Fire Department, Sanitation Department and his alma mater, Manhattan College.
Missing from the election-year parade were three Democrats seeking to challenge the Republican mayor for his job in November.

Manhattan Borough President Ruth Messinger, Bronx Borough President Fernando Ferrer and the Rev. Al Sharpton all said they would not join the parade because its organisers, a Roman Catholic group called the Ancient Order of Hibernians, have refused to let a gay and lesbian group march.
Giuliani, who marches each year, said: "This is a parade about Irish pride, and June is the Gay and Lesbian Pride parade. They'll have a chance to demonstrate their pride."

Members of the group, the Irish Lesbian and Gay Organisation, held a small protest on Fifth Avenue before the parade began. Thirty-five were arrested on charges of disorderly conduct or resisting arrest.

Also on hand was a group called Friends of Roisin McAliskey. McAliskey, a pregnant bombing suspect in prison in London, is fighting extradition to Germany, where she is wanted on charges connected to an Irish Republican Army bombing of a British Army barracks.
She is the daughter of the former Bernadette Devlin, a key figure in the Irish republican movement.
Scheduled to view the event with the Roman Catholic cardinal were the parents of Patrick McNeill, a 21-year-old Fordham University student who has been missing for a month.

Friends last saw him at a bar on Manhattan's Upper East Side on Feb. 16. Hundreds of posters seeking information on his whereabouts hang on lampposts and in shop windows all over New York City and its suburbs.
